source_gaps: Apple and Google pages were read through a summarising WebFetch; step wording is captured with labels quoted but was not checked character by character, so the excerpts should be compared with the live page. The Apple page gives no iOS version. The Google page says the Personal Safety app is on some Android devices and that Emergency SOS needs Android 12 or later; the supervised-user Family Link condition (each contact must be added as a Parent Managed Contact) was seen and deliberately not used. No iPhone emergency-contact steps were found on the Apple page, so no iPhone contact ref exists.

source_refs.title: Set up your Medical ID in the Health app on your iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the page states no iOS version; Enhanced Emergency Data is not available in all countries or regions
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Medical ID helps first responders access your critical medical information from the Lock screen
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open the Health app and tap the Summary tab. Tap your profile picture in the upper corner. Under your profile picture, tap 'Medical ID'. Turn on 'Show When Locked' to make Medical ID available from the Lock screen. Tap 'Edit' or 'Add' next to a field to update it. You can add medications, allergies, and conditions. Tap 'Done'.

source_refs.title: Set up your Medical ID in the Health app on your iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Share Medical ID during an emergency call and the Emergency Calls & SOS condition
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; Enhanced Emergency Data is not available in all countries or regions
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To share your Medical ID with emergency responders, turn on Share During Emergency Call.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: To share your Medical ID with emergency responders, turn on 'Share During Emergency Call'. Medical ID is then shared automatically when you call or text emergency services from iPhone or Apple Watch. If you turn off 'Emergency Calls & SOS', your Medical ID information will not be shared. This is set under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services.

source_refs.title: Get help during an emergency with your Android phone - Android Help
source_refs.applicability: Android; the Personal Safety app is available on some Android devices and appears in the app list as 'Safety'; Emergency SOS needs Android 12 or later
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To show your emergency information when your screen is locked, tap Emergency info access and then Show when locked.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Open the Safety app and sign in to your Google Account. Tap 'Your info'. Tap 'Medical information', then tap an item such as blood type, allergies, or medications to update it. For contacts, tap 'Emergency contacts' and then 'Add contact'. Choose the existing contact you want to add. To show your emergency information when your screen is locked, tap 'Emergency info access' and then 'Show when locked'.

source_refs.section: Viewing emergency info on a locked screen; sharing with emergency services; who can see it
source_refs.applicability: Android; the Personal Safety app is available on some Android devices
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Anyone who picks up your phone can find your lock screen message and emergency information even if your phone is locked.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: On a locked screen, swipe up. Tap 'Emergency' and then 'View emergency info'. To share with emergency services, open the Personal Safety app, tap 'Your info', then 'Emergency Info access', and then 'Share during emergency call'. Anyone who picks up your phone can find your lock screen message and emergency information even if your phone is locked. You can turn this setting off in the Safety app.
